newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares spurred ahead on Monday and closed once more at a record, with financials, Unilever, KPN and Internatio-Muller among the big gainers.
AEX share index closed 12.50 points higher at 731.99.
Dealers said the strong dollar, low interest rates, low inflation and the publication recently of good profits from some companies were boosting business.

Consumer products group Unilever jumped 16.20 guilders to a new record of 367.20. Last week the stock had gained some 40 guilders already, since it reported strong results and announced it was to divest its chemicals business.
Dealers said it was also the strong dollar that supported Unilever. The dollar rose to 1.9071 guilders at the close versus 1.8972 in early trade.
The strong dollar was also good for Ahold, the financials and Royal Dutch. Dealers said the outlook for the Dutch share market remained positive. "The trend is still up," said one.
ABN AMRO jumped 3.50 guilders to 133.60. Dealers said it was in demand on rumours that its 1996 results will be better than expected.
All financials closed at a new record. ING was up 1.40 guilders at 73.50 and Fortis Amev rose 1.80 guilders 72.50.
Dutch Telecom KPN closed 2.50 guilders higher at 70.60 and dealers said the liberalisation of the world's telephone markets, as agreed by World Trade Organisation members, would not hurt it.
"There is no concern for KPN," said one dealer. On the local market carbon maker Norit outperformed other stocks by far as investors welcomed Friday's results and outlook for the company.
Norit reported a profit rise to 18.5 million guilders in 1996 from 11.0 million guilders in 1995.
The stock rose 6.80 guilders to 34.00 in heavy volume.
Computer services group Getronics closed up one guilder at a high of 64.40. Baan, also in the high tech sector, shed 1.40 guilders to 94.00.
